narrative.intro: Total federal contract obligations are $403B for FY2026 to date. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction is the largest NAICS market with $40.6B in obligations. Aircraft Manufacturing and Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers each have $34.6B in obligations. Engineering Services follows with $32.4B, Facilities Support Services with $31.3B, and Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) with $28.2B. Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing has $25.9B in obligations. Computer Systems Design Services accounts for $20B, Ship Building and Repairing accounts for $16.5B, and Other Computer Related Services accounts for $14.4B. The ranking shows construction, aerospace, health insurance, engineering, and support services among the largest NAICS categories buying from the federal government so far this fiscal year. The totals are fiscal year to date and represent contract obligations rather than completed spending. Contractors and analysts should treat these figures as partial-year obligations when comparing to full-year totals or planning capacity.

sections.heading: Which NAICS industries lead federal contracting this fiscal year?
sections.body: Commercial and Institutional Building Construction leads federal contracting with $40.6B in obligations. Aircraft Manufacturing and Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers tie with $34.6B each. Engineering Services and Facilities Support Services follow with $32.4B and $31.3B respectively.

sections.heading: How concentrated are federal obligations across the top NAICS markets?
sections.body: The top ten NAICS markets together account for large single-industry obligations within the $403B total. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences has $28.2B, Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing has $25.9B, and Computer Systems Design Services has $20B, showing significant allocations across multiple sectors.

faq.q: What are the biggest federal contracting industries?
faq.a: The biggest federal contracting industries are Commercial and Institutional Building Construction ($40.6B), Aircraft Manufacturing ($34.6B), and Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers ($34.6B). Engineering Services ($32.4B), Facilities Support Services ($31.3B), and Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) ($28.2B) are also among the largest, with Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing ($25.9B), Computer Systems Design Services ($20B), Ship Building and Repairing ($16.5B), and Other Computer Related Services ($14.4B) rounding out the top ten.
